OK-governor.statusNote: Open seat (Gov. Stitt term-limited). The June 16 GOP primary went to an Aug 25 runoff: Attorney General Gentner Drummond and former state Sen. Mike Mazzei each took just over 25% in a nine-candidate field, so the Republican nominee is not final. House Minority Leader Cyndi Munson won the Democratic nomination June 16 with 75.1%.

candidates.name: Gentner Drummond
candidates.background: Oklahoma Attorney General since 2023; former Air Force F-15 pilot who flew 32 combat missions in the Gulf War, Osage County rancher, banking lawyer, and principal owner of Blue Sky Bank. Led the June 16 primary with just over 25% and faces Mike Mazzei in the Aug 25 Republican runoff.
priorities: Crack down on cartels and support law enforcement

cost.label: Would lower costs by confronting insurance companies and corporations rather than through broad tax cuts (News9 candidate guide)

immigration.label: 'Strong supporter of President Trump's border policies', tougher immigration enforcement and cooperation with federal authorities (News9 candidate guide)

taxes.label: 'Cut taxes responsibly without sacrificing schools, roads, or public safety', with property tax relief (campaign issues)

climate.label: Joined Republican AGs opposing the lesser prairie-chicken endangered listing and Biden administration changes to the 'waters of the United States' rule, and sued the EPA over ozone regulations (Wikipedia)

education.label: Education plan invests in public schools: reading proficiency by 3rd grade, CareerTech and apprenticeship expansion, incentivizing teachers (campaign issues)

safety.label: 'Crack down on cartel activity and drug trafficking' and 'support and strengthen local law enforcement' (campaign issues)

repro.label: As AG sued the Biden administration for suspending Oklahoma's Title X grant after the state declined to provide abortion referrals, defending the state's pro-life policies (Oklahoma AG press release)

democracy.label: In a DOJ voter-data settlement touted Oklahoma's proof-of-identity requirement, absentee ballot notarization, and ballot harvesting ban, pledging cooperation 'to eliminate voter fraud' (Oklahoma AG press release)

nullNotes.health: campaign healthcare plank is cost-focused (price transparency, rural hospital partnerships, holding insurers accountable) with no stance on public versus private coverage role; Ballotpedia and Wikipedia also empty on this axis; record search also empty (his AG letter calling Stitt's Medicaid managed care 'an abject, systemic failure' is an operational critique that also disparages Obamacare, not a coverage-role stance)
nullNotes.housing: checked campaign issues page, Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, News9 candidate guide; property tax relief is his only housing-adjacent item and it does not fit the axis; record search also empty (his OHFA letter concerns appointee removal, not housing policy)

candidates.name: Mike Mazzei
candidates.now: Financial planner; founder and president of The Financial Coach, Inc.
candidates.background: Former state senator for the Bixby area (2004-2016) who twice chaired the Senate Finance Committee, and Gov. Stitt's first Secretary of Budget. Founder of a Tulsa financial planning firm. Advanced to the Aug 25 Republican runoff with just over 25% on June 16; endorsed by President Trump per his campaign site.
priorities: Eliminate the state income tax in phases
Lower the cost of living for families

cost.label: 'Lower the cost of living for families' by cutting taxes and making government live within its means (campaign issues)

immigration.label: Pledges prosecuting criminals and deporting undocumented immigrants, plus stronger action against cartels and foreign influence (KOSU)

taxes.label: Three-phase plan to eliminate the state income tax, starting with a cut from 4.75% to 3.25%; calls the tax code 'a giant octopus' (KOSU)

education.label: Mixed: up to $150 million for phonics-based reading programs and a statewide literacy director, while vowing to remove 'woke ideology' from classrooms (KOSU)

safety.label: Targets 'Mexican cartels and illegal marijuana operations' as top public safety priorities (News9 candidate guide)

repro.label: 'Life begins at conception'; opposes abortion in all circumstances (campaign issues)

nullNotes.health: checked campaign issues page, KOSU launch coverage, Ballotpedia, News9 candidate guide; no healthcare stance documented; record search also empty (no roll calls from his 2004-2016 Senate service surfaced in fetched sources)
nullNotes.housing: his 'no Oklahoman should be taxed out of their home' plank is senior and veteran property tax relief, not a build-versus-protect housing stance; checked campaign site, KOSU, Ballotpedia; record search also empty
nullNotes.climate: checked campaign issues page, KOSU launch coverage, Ballotpedia, News9 candidate guide; no energy or climate stance documented; record search also empty (Wikipedia and Ballotpedia list no energy votes from his Senate service)
nullNotes.democracy: checked campaign issues page, KOSU launch coverage, Ballotpedia, News9 candidate guide; no election-law stance documented; record search also empty (his individual vote on Oklahoma's 2009 voter ID referral could not be documented in any fetched source)

candidates.name: Cyndi Munson
candidates.background: Oklahoma House minority leader and the first Asian American elected to the Oklahoma Legislature; daughter of a Vietnam veteran and a South Korean immigrant mother, and a first-generation college graduate. Worked in nonprofits before winning her Oklahoma City House seat in 2015. Won the June 16 Democratic primary with 75.1%.
priorities: Public school funding and teacher raises
Lower healthcare and prescription drug costs
Let voters repeal the abortion ban

health.label: Backs Oklahoma's voter-approved Medicaid expansion covering roughly 200,000 working Oklahomans; would cut drug and premium costs (KOSU)

immigration.label: As House minority leader opposed HB 4156 making unlawful presence a state crime, calling it 'extremist legislation' offering 'false hope and false solutions' (Oklahoma Voice)

education.label: Bring public school funding over the regional average, raise pay for public school teachers and staff, and end the voucher program sending public dollars to private schools (campaign priorities)

safety.label: Emphasizes 'prevention and addressing root causes of crime' through mental health services (News9 candidate guide)

repro.label: Would 'send the repeal of the abortion ban to a vote of the people' (campaign priorities)
